claims.text: The initial material is a single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy.
Introducing a secondary phase into a single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy will increase its coercive field.
Refining the grains of a single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy will increase its coercive field.
A secondary phase increases coercivity by pinning domain walls.
Grain-size reduction suppresses magnetization reversal and thereby increases coercivity.
The intervention will produce a coercive field greater than 100 Oe relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a derivative.
Single-phase fcc FeCoNi and its high-entropy-alloy derivatives have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe.
The applicable structural boundary includes an fcc matrix with possible secondary phases or refined grains.
The applicable measurement boundary is magnetic hysteresis-loop measurement of coercive field.
The optimal phase structure, microstructure, and processing conditions for maximizing coercivity are unknown.

contradictions.description: The requested intervention is not singular: secondary-phase introduction and grain refinement are distinct interventions, are joined by 'or,' and would require separate controlled tests.

The prediction uses an absolute coercivity threshold of >100 Oe, whereas the falsification rule describes 'no significant increase' and then places >100 Oe in parentheses, conflating an absolute threshold with a relative or statistical increase.
